title: Operational Context Corpus for Autonomous Systems
description:
A reproducible pipeline and corpus linking real PX4 flight telemetry to the external operating conditions under which it was produced, with a queryable schema and full provenance. A machine-readable operational-design-domain representation is in scope and not yet built.

First result. An agreement analysis between ERA5 reanalysis wind and onboard PX4 EKF2 wind estimates over 871 flights and 1,059 run-hours. We find no evidence of a systematic component-wise offset between the reanalysis and the onboard estimate — every component bias interval includes zero, which is a failure to reject rather than a demonstration of equivalence — and agreement is far too imprecise for the reanalysis to substitute for the onboard estimate, with limits of agreement near ±5 m s-1 per component. It is not a useful proxy in any regime tested, under a criterion fixed before the result existed. See docs/10-h1-results.md.

What this deposit contains. The pipeline, the JSON Schemas, the architecture decision records, and the aggregate analysis artifacts with the AnalysisManifest attesting each one. Every published number traces to a manifest recording input hashes, dependency versions, parameters, seeds and retrieval timestamps.

What it does not contain. No raw ULog files, no geolocated trajectories, and no per-run rows carrying a positional attribute. Positional results are published only in aggregate, at no fewer than 20 runs and 10 distinct vehicles per cell, with suppressed cells reported alongside their counts. The source logs remain public at PX4 Flight Review; this deposit is the pipeline and the results, not a redistribution of the corpus. See PRIVACY.md, DATA_LICENSES.md and docs/09-dpia.md.

Code is Apache-2.0. The external data sources carry their own terms and attribution requirements, which are recorded in DATA_LICENSES.md and travel with any derived product.
